records.context: tiled segmentation (:func:`segment_tiled`): microscope image fields of ``seg_tile_px`` with ``seg_tile_overlap_px`` of overlap, segmented in row-major order; copies of one object in two microscope image fields are merged by IoU, keeping the copy whose centroid is farther from an inner microscope image field edge (:func:`stitch_tile_labels`); a site no larger than one microscope image field goes through the segmenter unchanged; each image data channel is normalised once on the whole site (:func:`normalize_site`) and the microscope image fields are segmented with ``normalize=False``, so a microscope image field sees the same values as the untiled site, and microscope image fields are placed on Cellpose's own network-microscope image field grid (:func:`tiling_layout`), so the network sees the same pixels tiled and untiled;

records.context: Tiles whose sides have evenly spaced network tiles (stride ``s``) and whose starts are multiples of ``s`` all run Cellpose's network on the same network tiles as the untiled image would: a pixel at least ``NET_TILE_PX`` from a cut tile edge then gets bit-identical flows tiled and untiled. Holds for Cellpose's defaults (``bsize=256``, ``tile_overlap=0.1``) and no resizing, that is no ``diameter``.
records.label: spacr.ops_large_sites.aligned_tiling#1
records.source: Tiles whose sides have evenly spaced network tiles (stride ``s``) and whose starts are multiples of ``s`` all run Cellpose's network on the same network tiles as the untiled image would: a pixel at least ``NET_TILE_PX`` from a cut tile edge then gets bit-identical flows tiled and untiled. Holds for Cellpose's defaults (``bsize=256``, ``tile_overlap=0.1``) and no resizing, that is no ``diameter``.
records.translation: Los mosaicos cuyos lados tienen mosaicos de red espaciados de forma regular (paso ``s``) y cuyos inicios son múltiplos de ``s`` ejecutan la red de Cellpose sobre los mismos mosaicos de red que la imagen sin mosaicos: un píxel situado al menos a ``NET_TILE_PX`` de un borde cortado de mosaico recibe entonces flujos idénticos bit a bit con y sin mosaicos. Vale para los valores por defecto de Cellpose (``bsize=256``, ``tile_overlap=0.1``) y sin redimensionar, es decir, sin ``diameter``.

records.context: The region is the largest side no larger than ``side`` whose network microscope image fields fall on one grid, and the microscope image field the smallest side on the same grid that covers the region in two microscope image fields per axis with at least ``overlap_px`` of overlap, so tiled and untiled runs share every network microscope image field away from the seams (:func:`aligned_tiling`). Without such a pair the region is ``side`` and the microscope image field ``(side + overlap_px) // 2 + 1``, unaligned.
records.label: spacr.ops_large_sites.control_layout#1
records.source: The region is the largest side no larger than ``side`` whose network tiles fall on one grid, and the tile the smallest side on the same grid that covers the region in two tiles per axis with at least ``overlap_px`` of overlap, so tiled and untiled runs share every network tile away from the seams (:func:`aligned_tiling`). Without such a pair the region is ``side`` and the tile ``(side + overlap_px) // 2 + 1``, unaligned.
records.translation: La región es el mayor lado no mayor que ``side`` cuyos mosaicos de red caen sobre una misma rejilla, y el mosaico es el menor lado sobre esa misma rejilla que cubre la región con dos mosaicos por eje y al menos ``overlap_px`` de solapamiento, de modo que las ejecuciones con y sin mosaicos comparten cada mosaico de red lejos de las costuras (:func:`aligned_tiling`). Sin tal pareja, la región es ``side`` y el mosaico ``(side + overlap_px) // 2 + 1``, sin alinear.

records.context: Cellpose pads an image to a multiple of 16 plus 8 px on each side and spreads ``ceil((1 + 2 * overlap) * padded / bsize)`` network tiles evenly over the padded side (``cellpose.core.run_net`` without resizing). records.source: Cellpose pads an image to a multiple of 16 plus 8 px on each side and spreads ``ceil((1 + 2 * overlap) * padded / bsize)`` network tiles evenly over the padded side (``cellpose.core.run_net`` without resizing). A pixel's flows are the tapered mean of the network tiles that cover it, so two runs give a pixel the same flows only when the same network tiles, with the same pixels, cover it.
records.translation: Cellpose rellena una imagen hasta un múltiplo de 16 más 8 px por cada lado y reparte ``ceil((1 + 2 * overlap) * padded / bsize)`` mosaicos de red de forma uniforme sobre el lado rellenado (``cellpose.core.run_net`` sin redimensionar). Los flujos de un píxel son la media atenuada de los mosaicos de red que lo cubren, así que dos ejecuciones dan a un píxel los mismos flujos solo cuando lo cubren los mismos mosaicos de red, con los mismos píxeles.

records.context: Cellpose's percentile normalisation, computed once on a whole site.
records.label: spacr.ops_large_sites.normalize_site#0
records.source: Cellpose's percentile normalisation, computed once on a whole site.
records.translation: La normalización por percentiles de Cellpose, calculada una sola vez sobre un sitio completo.

records.context: Cellpose normalises every image it is given, so a microscope image field is scaled by its own 1st and 99th percentiles and the same pixel gets different values in two microscope image fields and in the untiled site. Here the percentiles of each image data channel come from the whole site, with the arithmetic of Cellpose's ``normalize_img`` (``normalize99`` with its subsampling; a flat image data channel becomes zeros), and every microscope image field is then segmented with ``normalize=False``. A site that fits in one microscope image field gets exactly the values Cellpose would have computed itself.
records.label: spacr.ops_large_sites.normalize_site#1
records.source: Cellpose normalises every image it is given, so a tile is scaled by its own 1st and 99th percentiles and the same pixel gets different values in two tiles and in the untiled site. Here the percentiles of each channel come from the whole site, with the arithmetic of Cellpose's ``normalize_img`` (``normalize99`` with its subsampling; a flat channel becomes zeros), and every tile is then segmented with ``normalize=False``. A site that fits in one tile gets exactly the values Cellpose would have computed itself.
records.translation: Cellpose normaliza cada imagen que recibe, de modo que un mosaico se escala con sus propios percentiles 1 y 99 y el mismo píxel recibe valores distintos en dos mosaicos y en el sitio sin mosaicos. Aquí los percentiles de cada canal proceden del sitio completo, con la aritmética de ``normalize_img`` de Cellpose (``normalize99`` con su submuestreo; un canal plano pasa a ceros), y después cada mosaico se segmenta con ``normalize=False``. Un sitio que cabe en un mosaico recibe exactamente los valores que Cellpose habría calculado por sí mismo.

records.context: The laboratory microplate's nucleus diameter and the tiling-control site from a sample of sites.
records.label: spacr.ops_large_sites.survey_sites#0

records.translation: El diámetro nuclear de la placa y el sitio del control de mosaicos a partir de una muestra de sitios.

records.context: A microplate sample position's first site is often an empty corner of the microplate sample position, so neither the diameter nor the tiling control may come from it. A sampled site counts only when it holds at least ``min_objects`` nuclei; the diameter is the median equivalent diameter over every nucleus of those sites, clipped to ``bounds`` (:func:`estimate_nucleus_diameter`), and the control site is the one with the median nucleus count among them (the lower of the two middle sites when their number is even).
records.label: spacr.ops_large_sites.survey_sites#1
records.source: A well's first site is often an empty corner of the well, so neither the diameter nor the tiling control may come from it. A sampled site counts only when it holds at least ``min_objects`` nuclei; the diameter is the median equivalent diameter over every nucleus of those sites, clipped to ``bounds`` (:func:`estimate_nucleus_diameter`), and the control site is the one with the median nucleus count among them (the lower of the two middle sites when their number is even).
records.translation: El primer sitio de un pocillo suele ser una esquina vacía del pocillo, así que ni el diámetro ni el control de mosaicos pueden proceder de él. Un sitio muestreado solo cuenta cuando contiene al menos ``min_objects`` núcleos; el diámetro es la mediana del diámetro equivalente de todos los núcleos de esos sitios, recortada a ``bounds`` (:func:`estimate_nucleus_diameter`), y el sitio de control es el que tiene el recuento mediano de núcleos entre ellos (el menor de los dos sitios centrales cuando su número es par).
